clue.text: Cold heralds decay on plant

indicators.note: to herald is to come before, so the cold letter goes in front of what follows

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to decay is to rot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener notices the chill arriving just before a plant starts to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Croton is a genus of tropical shrubs, also the name of a popular variegated houseplant.

clue.text: Press reporting makes chap feel angry

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a fellow or chap
to rage is to feel or show anger

explanation.surface: A man is furious about what the newspapers are saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Media treatment of a news story is the amount it is reported.

clue.text: Impound ecstasy distributed in drug-filled environment

indicators.note: letters that are distributed are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Police seize ecstasy that was being dealt in a drug den.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a place where opium is smoked, a narcotic haunt.

clue.text: Deep love can stifle one in the end

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: the can word smothers the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Deep love may smother a person eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' takes E from 'one'; 'stifle' puts it inside CAN after O.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic name for the sea.

clue.text: Criminals don't allow song to be heard

indicators.note: the clue asks for words as they sound when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: to ban is to forbid or not allow; a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Someone forbids a tune from being performed out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: BAN DITTY spoken sounds like the Italian-derived plural for a gang of outlaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is an old plural of bandit, meaning outlaws or robbers.

clue.text: Performing such a role in stage musical

definitions.text: Performing such a role in stage musical

parts.words: Performing such a role in stage musical
parts.note: a dancer in a line of backing singers would be performing that role in this Broadway show

explanation.surface: An actor takes a part in a theatrical musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of the 1975 Broadway musical describes the ensemble's role.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical is named for a row of ensemble dancers and singers.

clue.text: Laughs a lot, given large Scotch to drink?

definitions.meaning: a double is a large measure of spirits, and serving up is giving to drink

explanation.definitionFit: Bending over with laughter, or literally serving up double measures of whisky.

clue.text: During strike one associates with an Oriental business chief

indicators.note: the letter for one comes during the strike word, inside it

parts.note: to tap is to strike lightly
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: During a strike, one person sides with a foreign business leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associates with' merely joins TAIP to AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A taipan is a powerful foreign merchant or tycoon in China or Hong Kong.

clue.text: Artist using restored frames

indicators.note: the two words act as a frame holding a run of letters

explanation.surface: A painter works on restored picture frames.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter.

clue.text: Live broadcast journalist covered

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of live are thrown into a new order

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter covers a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns LIVE into VEIL, then ED follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something veiled is hidden or concealed, as under a cloth.

clue.text: Before trip, she's not finished crying

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed before the word for the trip
a word that is not finished loses its final letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
an outing is a short excursion or trip

explanation.surface: She is in tears before setting off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' trims SHE to SH, and 'Before' puts it in front of OUTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying out loudly is yelling; crying here is calling out, not weeping.

clue.text: A cow, I think

parts.note: a cow chews the cud, and someone who says I think is pondering things over; both chew things over

explanation.surface: Someone tentatively identifies an animal in a field as a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hesitant guess; really both a cud-chewing cow and a person musing are ones who mull things over.
explanation.definitionFit: One who ruminates either chews the cud like cattle or meditates deeply.

clue.text: Mischievous book written about change in Russia

indicators.note: the book word is written around the money word, enclosing it

parts.note: a tome is a large book
roubles are Russian currency, the change in your pocket there

explanation.surface: A naughty book is written about political change in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like reform but is money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing difficulty or bother is a nuisance, close to naughty.

clue.text: Holiday area in mostly flat environment

indicators.note: the area letter goes inside the shortened word for flat
mostly means almost all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: level means flat or even

explanation.surface: A holiday area set in flat, open surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LEVEL to LEVE; 'in ... environment' places A inside it. Leave is time off work, as in annual leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is permitted absence from work, a vacation.

clue.text: Believes you could be accommodated inside … these?

indicators.note: one word is housed within another, so the word for you sits inside the first

parts.note: guesses means supposes or believes
thou is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Someone believes you might find lodging in these places.
explanation.walkthrough: THOU, old-fashioned 'you', is put inside GUESSES; the definition 'these' points back to places where you are accommodated.
explanation.definitionFit: Small lodging houses where paying visitors are put up for the night.

clue.text: Ended up being expelled

definitions.meaning: finished in a certain state, proved to be

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both proved in the end and kicked out.

clue.text: Short examination one finished, securing pass grade

indicators.note: the words for one and finished hold the grade letter securely inside

parts.note: taken as written
C is a passing grade in exams
over means ended or finished

explanation.surface: One quick test is over, with a pass grade secured.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look-through is a brief inspection.

clue.text: Court gives opportunist a year

parts.note: a chancer is British slang for someone who takes risky chances

explanation.surface: A court sentences an opportunist to a year.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANCER is British slang for a reckless opportunist. Chancery is a division of England's High Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court of Justice.

clue.text: Teacher has little time to get a drink — that's a blow

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
T is the abbreviation for time
punch is a mixed drink, often fruity and alcoholic

explanation.surface: A teacher grabs a quick drink, and someone remarks it's a knock to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit punch is a sharp chop to the back of the neck.

clue.text: Opera still listened to in French

indicators.note: the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: calm means still or tranquil
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: An opera is still heard in French.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent CALM sounds like CARM; then EN, French for 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's opera is named after a Spanish gypsy heroine.

clue.text: Scout wanders near North American city

indicators.note: wanders means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A scout wanders close to a North American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanders' turns SCOUT into TUCSO; 'near' just joins N. 'North American city' looks like a single unit, but N comes from 'North'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucson is a city in Arizona.

clue.text: Colour of sky in distant continent, do you say?

indicators.note: the question asks whether the word sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: Asia is a continent far from Britain

explanation.surface: Is the sky a different colour on a faraway continent?
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken with a non-rhotic British accent, the continent and the blue shade sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright clear blue, the hue of a cloudless sky.

clue.text: Will Young hit making one pine?

definitions.meaning: Will Young is a British pop singer whose first single was a 2002 chart-topper
a pine is a tree that keeps its needles all year

explanation.surface: A pop single that makes someone pine.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Young won the British TV talent show Pop Idol; 'pine' looks like a verb (to long) but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is a tree that keeps foliage year-round, and Will Young's debut single bore that name.

clue.text: Good book for a girl

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A good book to give a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemma is a female first name.

clue.text: Fox kept by builder is very old creature

indicators.note: the fox word is held inside the builder word

parts.note: a mason builds with stone
tod is an old dialect word for a fox

explanation.surface: A builder keeps a fox, which turns out to be a prehistoric beast.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD, a northern English dialect word for a fox, goes inside MASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastodon is an extinct elephant-like mammal from millions of years ago.

clue.text: Film mob's terrible struggle

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of the gang word are mangled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A film about a gang's awful fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns MOB into BMO, then VIE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A B-movie is a low-budget film, originally the second feature.

clue.text: Einstein laboured for several years

indicators.note: laboured suggests the letters were worked over into another form

explanation.surface: The physicist toiled for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade such as 1990 to 1999 spans several years.

clue.text: Absolutely not how cheats play

definitions.meaning: in the sense of positively, as in being quite literally bursting with pride
cheats do not play honestly or by the rules

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both utterly or positively, and honestly or justly.
